paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to hold onto. David had Saul asleep at his feet, the spear stuck in the ground, and his own man saying, "Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand" (1 Samuel 26:8). It looked like the perfect moment, and David still said no. His reason was simple: "who can extend a hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?" (1 Samuel 26:9).

So the lesson is this. A door swinging wide open doesn't mean God wants you to walk through it. David didn't take matters into his own hands. He said, "the LORD Himself will strike him down" (1 Samuel 26:10). He trusted God to settle it in His own time, and that's the hardest kind of waiting there is. I once waited on a batch with a timer and still opened that oven early, so I know how hard it is!

And look at how David asks God to treat him: "As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble" (1 Samuel 26:24). He leaves his rescue with God. Baker, when someone wrongs you and you finally have the upper hand, this passage is for that moment. Do right, and trust God with the rest. The story isn't over, so stay close to the oven.
